decisions.reason: Although no longer visible as a standalone website item, it remains tightly tied to our core second-channel authentication know-how, so we are more likely to retain or embed it in the platform than withdraw it completely.

We have strong related knowledge in digital signing, but the lack of recent visibility and the shift from PDF-specific functions toward broader signing workflows make withdrawal of the standalone offer more likely.
This architecture sits at the heart of our cryptography and platform capabilities, so our absorptive capacity is highest here and favors continued development rather than exit.
As a narrower use case built on our communication stack, it is easier to absorb its learning into broader secure messaging solutions than to keep marketing it as a separate product.

The hardware-based token is related to our security expertise but is less central to our software-led identity strategy and, without visible recent traction, is the strongest candidate for withdrawal.
